To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
myocardial infarction is a progressive process, and that the collateral circulation is not a major factor in the process.

the collateral circulation in the monkey is a high-pressure system that is capable of maintaining a normal pressure gradient between the aorta and the occluded coronary artery during myocardial infarction.

the myocardium of the monkey, like that of the dog, is capable of maintaining a normal blood flow during the first 12 hr of acute coronary occlusion; that the myocardial flow falls by 50% at 24 hr, but thereafter remains constant for several days, even though infarction is progressing rapidly; that collateral circulation is well developed in the monkey, and that the pressures transmitted through collateral channels to the occluded artery do not change during the period of developing infar
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of new methods for the detection of myocardial infarction.
the effects of acute coronary occlusion on myocardial flow, pressure transmission through collaterals, and infarct development.
the effects of the environment on the growth and development of the organism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

myocardial infarction is a process of ischemia and necrosis, the latter being the result of a failure of the collateral circulation to maintain adequate perfusion pressure in the occluded coronary vessels.
in the monkey the development of infarction is not dependent on the presence of an adequate coronary collateral circulation.

the collateral circulation is a significant factor in the maintenance of the viability of the ischemic myocardium in the early period following acute coronary occlusion and that it plays a relatively minor role in the late period of infarct development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in monkeys, as in man, the collateral circulation is not a major factor in the development of infarction, but it does maintain a high pressure through the distal coronary bed during the development of infraction.
the collateral circulation is of limited importance in the early stages after acute coronary occlusions, but it may become more significant in the later stages.

the collateral circulation is of great importance in the monkey and is capable of maintaining a high pressure distal to the site of occlusion for a period of time after ligation, but that it is not able to sustain the flow required to maintain the viability of the myocardium.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use the same techniques to measure coronary blood flow in monkeys that we use in dogs and pigs.
the monkey is a suitable animal for studies on collateral circulation and myocardial infarction.
the collateral circulation in the dog and monkey is a dynamic entity, and its development is not complete for at least 3 weeks after ligation.
